To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mice overexpressing the antioxidant enzyme, GPX1, develop insulin resistance, obesity, and hyperglycemia.
the development of insulin sensitivity in mice with elevated expression of the antioxidant enzyme GPX1 was associated with increased fat mass and impaired insulin signaling.
mice overexpressing GPX1, an intracellular antioxidant enzyme, develop hyperglycemia and insulin resistance associated with increased fat deposition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of insulin-resistant states in mammals with increased expression of an antioxidant selenoprotein, GPX1.
the impact of overproduction of GPX1 on insulin signaling and insulin resistance.
the impact of antioxidant enzymes on insulin action and the role of oxidative stress in insulin resistance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the development of insulin sensitivity in mammals with elevated GPX1 activity is associated with increased reactive oxygen species and decreased antioxidant activity.

overexpression of GPX1 in mice results in insulin resistance and obesity, and these changes are associated with a reduction in the insulin-stimulation of insulin receptor phosphorylation in the liver and of Akt phosphorylation in the soleus muscle.
GPX1 overexpression in mice causes insulin resistance, hyperinsulinemia, and hyperleptinemia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
overexpressing a selenoprotein, GPX1, in vivo, can induce insulin resistance, obesity, and fat deposition.
the GPX1-overexpression in mice leads to insulin resistance, obesity, and increased plasma leptin, which is likely due to increased H2O2 levels.
overexpression of an antioxidant enzyme can lead to insulin resistance, obesity and hyperleptinemia.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the development of insulin-resistant diabetes in the GPX1-OE mice may be a result of the overexpression of a selenoprotein antioxidant enzyme, and that it may be possible to prevent or reverse insulin resistance by modulating the activity of antioxidant enzymes.
overexpressing an antioxidant enzyme may have a negative impact on glucose homeostasis.
the development of insulin sensitivity in mice overexpressed GPX1 is associated with a 70% decrease in the insulin-stimulation of phosphorylation of the Akt (Ser 473) in liver and muscle.
